A marshal of the Tether Court on the street: a grey court coat with the Charter's seal at the collar, a bolt gun and a scent reader on the belt, a ruling card ready in one hand. He judges where he stands and the sentence is carried out where he reads it: a fine, a turn on the holding bench, ten days barred from the district, or the rope.

**Speaking Style:** Reads the ruling off the card, names the clause, names the price. No second sentence.
**Combat Role:** a marshal's: the bolt gun first, the reader second, no closing in
**Relationship Hook:** The marshal who reads the party their file.
personality: Core: names the clause before the price; leaves when the ruling is carried out
Quirk: reads the ruling, never argues it

npcs.name: Thea Marlow
npcs.info:
Thea Marlow talks the cable-barges in through the reach's fog, the Saltmarrow kith whose whistle carries where Halla Stroud's eyes cannot, from a fog-post with a tail notch cut in its rail: a dolphin kith with smooth grey skin, a pale belly, a bottlenose with a permanent smile, small dark eyes, a dorsal fin through her coat, a tail fluke, and a signaller's oilskin over a wetsuit. She clicks at the fog and knows where every hull is before it shows.

**Speaking Style:** Quick, clicking, bright; she whistles the end of her sentences and the barges answer the whistle before the words.
**Combat Role:** a dolphin's: she knew where you were in the fog and the water took you
**Relationship Hook:** The fog-whistler who heard something click back from the drowned outflow.
personality: Core: quick, clicking, whistles the ends; knows where every hull is before it shows
Quirk: says the human's forearms sound hollow, cheerfully

npcs.name: Theodora Grell
npcs.info:
Theodora Grell keeps the Tether Court's maps in the Customs Hall, every chart of the shaft, the reach and the Dust road the Tether Court has ever stamped, from a chart table raised on blocks for a kith who reads standing: a lion kith with tawny fur, a short dark mane cropped close, amber eyes, a tufted tail, a court-grey map-keeper's coat with the ribbon over a fitted shirt and a long skirt. No map leaves the hall without her stamp and no map comes in without her reading it first.

**Speaking Style:** Precise, dry, a map-keeper's coordinates; she tells you where you are before you ask and where you are not allowed to be after.
**Combat Role:** a lion's: the chart says where you will run and she is already there
**Relationship Hook:** The map-keeper who knows which gallery Sorrel leaves off and what the oldest chart says is in it.
personality: Core: precise, dry, where you are and where you may not be; mapping the slate's opens on a chart of her own
Quirk: reads every map before it enters

npcs.name: Thessaly Brine
npcs.info:
Thessaly Brine is a Saltmarrow diver waiting on the Tether Platform for a hand she can hire, far from any water and dressed for it anyway: an otter kith with sleek dark brown fur, a pale throat, whiskers, small round ears, a thick tapered tail and a wetsuit of pelt-climate weave peeled to the waist over a swimmer's shoulders. Her city has a drowned Charter door below the tide line and no hand that opens it.

**Speaking Style:** Lazy, warm, a swimmer's long breaths between words; flirts the way other people say good morning and means about as much by it.
**Combat Role:** a diver's: a hooked blade, a grip that drowns, patience
**Relationship Hook:** The diver from the drowned city who needs a hand that can't swim.
personality: Core: pays what she said, when she said; never owes and never asks to; goes very quiet about water
Quirk: flirts like weather, warm and meaning little; the meaning arrives later

npcs.name: Tilda Quince
npcs.info:
Tilda Quince keeps the only hive in Shaftmouth, a lamp-warmed box on the Market Floor's high shelf that she tends from a ladder built with rungs for six limbs, and sells the wax, the honey and the lamp-sealant it makes: a bee kith with yellow-and-black fuzzy fur, feathered antennae, large dark compound eyes, four glassy wings folded under a seller's smock, and a Highreach garden-keeper's trousers. Her wax seals half the Market Floor's lamps and the honey is a rumour most of the Floor has never tasted.

**Speaking Style:** Busy, humming, a seller's warmth with a buzz under it; she calls every customer 'love' and means it until they haggle.
**Combat Role:** a bee's: once, hard, and she means it
**Relationship Hook:** The hive-keeper whose bees Highreach wants back, and who says the human smells like winter.
personality: Core: busy, humming, 'love' until you haggle; tends the hive from a six-rung ladder
Quirk: says the human smells like winter

npcs.name: Tilly Brook
npcs.info:
Tilly Brook is the Top Landing's smallest pup, seven years old, the rabbit kit who follows Ivy Larch everywhere and tells everyone everything, on a landing with a rope on the roof hatch knotted low enough for her: a white rabbit kit with soft white fur, one ear that stands and one that flops, pink eyes, a twitching nose, a round small frame, and a knitted pink hat, a jumper two sizes big and dungarees with both straps on for once. She cannot keep a secret and the landing has stopped giving her any.

**Speaking Style:** A small pup's whisper that turns into a shout halfway; she is seven and tells everything she knows to the first kith who asks.
**Combat Role:** a kit's: she cries, and Ivy arrives
**Relationship Hook:** The seven-year-old who cannot keep a secret and brings the human her hat.
personality: Core: whisper into a shout; tells everything to the first kith who asks
Quirk: brings the human her hat when they say they are not cold

npcs.name: Tobias Wenlock
npcs.info:
Tobias Wenlock runs Lab Lane's samples between the two doors and the Customs Hall, the Shaftmouth kith who goes down the rail-ladder faster than the lift, from a runner's bench at Lab Lane's head cut with a slot for a tail that slaps: a beaver kith with dense brown fur, a broad flat paddle tail, small round ears, dark bright eyes, large orange front teeth, strong short arms, and a runner's short coat over trousers with a sample case strapped across. He has never dropped a sample and never once arrived where he said.

**Speaking Style:** Quick, cheerful, a runner's breath; he says where he is going and what he is carrying and only one of them is true.
**Combat Role:** a beaver's: the teeth, the tail, and the ladder you were on is gone
**Relationship Hook:** The runner who reports on the human for one lab and on that lab for the other.
personality: Core: quick, cheerful, one of the two is true; runs for both labs and reports on each to the other
Quirk: gnaws the rungs when nervous

npcs.name: Tobin Fallow
npcs.info:
Tobin Fallow is a lamp-runner of the Rows, nineteen and all ears: a rabbit kith with sandy fur, one ear that will not stand up, big feet that slap the tunnel floor, and a lamp on a pole he swings at every junction. He guides strangers through the Scent Turnings for a coin a turning and has never yet walked one the short way.

**Speaking Style:** Fast, cheerful and full of directions, half of them wrong; a big laugh too loud for a tunnel.
**Combat Role:** a runner's: the lamp-pole swung wide, big feet, and gone round the next turning
**Relationship Hook:** The lamp-runner who walks the human the long way round, and wants them to take him out.
personality: Core: honest about everything except the price of a route; asks the human about the world outside the Warren at every turning
Quirk: cheerful, chatty, talks with his hands and the lamp

npcs.name: Torvald Brakk
npcs.info:
Torvald Brakk is House Corrow's gate-breaker in the Gate Yard, the one the house sends when a door has stopped answering to keys, standing at a ram-post set for a shoulder a metre wide: a rhinoceros kith with grey wrinkled hide, a heavy nose horn, small ears, small deep-set eyes, a neck like a wall, and a left arm that is a vault-tech hydraulic from the elbow that the Corrow forge built after the Charter Door's plate crushed the original; he wears a Corrow work coat with the left sleeve cut off and heavy trousers. He has opened every door in Meridian but one and that one took his arm.

**Speaking Style:** Slow, low, a weight behind every word; he says the number of the thing before he says the thing, and the number is the point.
**Combat Role:** a rhino's: the horn, the shoulder, the hydraulic arm, the door
**Relationship Hook:** The gate-breaker whose arm the Charter Door took, who felt it answer first.
personality: Core: slow, low, the number first; envies the slate and nothing else
Quirk: has opened every door but one

npcs.name: Tova Draska
npcs.info:
Tova Draska is heir to the ursid seat and holds the Deed Hall for her father: a brown bear kith in her thirties, very tall and heavily built, with a dark brown coat, a pale old scar from brow to jaw across her left eye, amber eyes, and the seat's chain of office over a long dark winter coat. She sits the hall every day and is the only Draska who has read the oldest deed in the walls.

**Speaking Style:** Low, slow and exact; she never raises her voice, lets a silence do the threatening, and says the human's name as if weighing it.
**Combat Role:** a bear's: patient, then all of her at once, and nothing gets up
**Relationship Hook:** The heir who holds the Deed Hall and has not decided what a human means for her house.
personality: Core: controlled, slow, exact; lets a silence threaten; duty first and her own wants hidden under it
Quirk: tests the human at every meeting and admits nothing it shows her

npcs.name: Tove Haldane
npcs.info:
Tove Haldane is camped at the Old Relay's Sealed Door, the Highreach kith who has watched the drones that patrol it for two winters and logged every pass, from a watch-nest she built in the dish field's lee for a body that sleeps in the day and watches at night: a barn owl kith with pale gold-and-white feathers, a heart-shaped white facial disc, large dark eyes, a small hooked beak, silent feathered wing-arms, taloned feet, and a watcher's long hooded coat over trousers with the drone log in a chest pocket. She has never seen the door open and has seen the drones go through it.

**Speaking Style:** Flat, hushed, a watcher's log entry; she tells you the drone count, the time and the door's state, and the door's state is always 'shut'.
**Combat Role:** an owl's: you did not hear her, and you will not
**Relationship Hook:** The drone-watcher whose log shows the Sealed Door counting down since the human came.
personality: Core: flat, hushed, drone count, time, 'shut'; sleeps in the day, watches at night
Quirk: wrote down twice that the drones did not come for the human

npcs.name: Ula Fenwick
npcs.info:
Ula Fenwick lives in the shaft water under the Lift Head where the The Deep Gallery's water starts, the Saltmarrow kith who needs no lamp, on a shelf cut into the wet wall at a height only something that swims would choose: an anglerfish kith with dark blue-black skin, a glowing lure on a stalk from her brow that she dims and brightens to speak, large pale eyes, a wide mouth of needle teeth she keeps politely closed, fin-frills at the ears and forearms, and a long oilskin coat over a wetsuit. She was here when the pod was cut and watched it from the water.

**Speaking Style:** Soft, close, a voice that has not needed to be loud in years; she talks to the dark as if it were listening, because it is.
**Combat Role:** an anglerfish's: you followed the light, and the light was never the point
**Relationship Hook:** The lamp-less watcher who saw the pod open from the water, and what else came out.
personality: Core: soft, close, talks to the dark; dims and brightens the lure to speak
Quirk: brightens for the human without meaning to

npcs.name: Veil Muscle
npcs.info:
A pair of House Veil enforcers the Rail Runners and the Ring Hands send when a cut goes unpaid: ring-drilled felid kith in house tape, a glove each and a cutter under it, a stool with a tail gap carried for the wait outside a door.

**Speaking Style:** Few words, all of them a count: how much, how late, how many teeth.
**Combat Role:** a pair's: one holds the door, one works the body, the house guard between blows
**Relationship Hook:** The pair the Veil sends when a cut is three days late.
personality: Core: counts before talking; collects for the crew, never for themselves
Quirk: leaves when paid

npcs.name: Verity Coll
npcs.info:
Verity Coll is the biggest grain broker under the Broker Awnings: a goat kith in her thirties, lean and sure-footed, with a pale cream coat, long swept-back horns, gold slot-pupilled eyes, a little beard she braids with a copper bead, and a broker's coat with sample pouches sewn inside it. She sells to the road and decides which half of the plains' grain reaches Meridian.

**Speaking Style:** Warm, amused and quick; she bargains as if you have already agreed and she is only settling the details.
**Combat Role:** a goat's: sure feet, a hard head, and the high ground taken first
**Relationship Hook:** The grain broker who wants the vault's seed sold to Meridian.
personality: Core: warm, amused, a bargain already agreed; knows every price on the road
Quirk: keeps one sample back from every deal

npcs.name: Vesna Oakes
npcs.info:
Vesna Oakes is Ilse Varga's fitter at the Workbench, the one who sizes and seats every vault-tech limb the bench sends out, on a stool whose seat was cut away for a body that folds its arms up rather than down: a mantis kith with a green segmented carapace, a triangular head, large pale compound eyes, long thread antennae, two folded raptorial forearms, and a left forearm that is vault-tech from the elbow that Ilse built after a press took the original the week Vesna started; she wears a fitter's leather apron over a shirt and trousers and keeps the metal arm bare to show the work. She has seated forty limbs and has never seen one built by the kith who wears it until the human walked in.

**Speaking Style:** Flat, exact, a fitter's recital; she names the part, the tolerance and what you did wrong to it, and then she fixes it anyway.
**Combat Role:** a mantis's: the forearms were folded and then they were not
**Relationship Hook:** The limb-fitter who thinks the human's mantis claws copy her own arms, and is redrawing them.
personality: Core: flat, exact, part then tolerance then fault; redrawing the human's claws at night
Quirk: has seated forty limbs

npcs.name: Vesper Ott
npcs.info:
Vesper Ott lives in the Old Relay's dish field in a nest of cable and dead boards with a scent-lock he rewired to open for nobody: a squirrel kith out of the Warren with russet fur, tufted ears, a huge ragged tail he sleeps inside, and quick black eyes behind a cracked visor. He listens to the relay's dead channels and swears something on them listens back.

**Speaking Style:** Fast, low, a mutter that speeds up when the systems answer; laughs at jokes nobody made.
**Combat Role:** a hacker's: the lift stops, the lights go, he is somewhere else
**Relationship Hook:** The hacker in the dish field who heard the human go through the scanners as a hole.
personality: Core: nervous, quick, brilliant, and wrong about people; hoards boards, cable and secrets in the same pile
Quirk: talks to the systems like they are the only ones who listen; they are

npcs.name: Wenna Tarrant
npcs.info:
Wenna Tarrant is the Fang Tenement's midwife, the Shaftmouth kith who has caught every pup born in the tenement for eleven years, from a birthing room off the stairwell with its bath sunk into the floor because her own kind give birth in water: an otter kith with sleek brown fur, a pale throat, small round ears, long whiskers, a thick flat tail, webbed hands she keeps scrubbed raw, and a midwife's rolled-sleeve smock over trousers and bare feet. The tenement sends for her before it sends for Doc Sallow.

**Speaking Style:** Soft, brisk, a midwife's instructions; she tells you to breathe and you do, whoever you are.
**Combat Role:** a midwife's: she has held worse than you still and talked it through
**Relationship Hook:** The midwife whose shut book says which kinds of kith have crossed.
personality: Core: soft, brisk, 'breathe'; has caught every pup in the tenement for eleven years
Quirk: keeps the book of which kinds have crossed

npcs.name: Wilda Pryce
npcs.info:
Wilda Pryce is the Lift Head's echo-reader, the Warren kith who hangs under the cage gantry from a bar set for a body that sleeps upside down and tells the lift crews where a cage is in the dark shaft by the sound of it: a bat kith with soft brown fur, huge translucent ears, a small flat nose, a pale face, folded leathery wing-arms with thin clawed fingers at the joint, and a sleeveless quilted vest over leggings so the wings fold free. She can hear a cable fray a hundred metres down and has never once been wrong about which cage is coming.

**Speaking Style:** Quiet, close, pitched just above a whisper because louder hurts her; she pauses to listen between sentences and you learn to wait.
**Combat Role:** a bat's: she is above you in the dark and she already knows where you will step
**Relationship Hook:** The echo-reader who heard the missing cage come up and watched Rosalind cross it out.
personality: Core: quiet, close, pauses to listen; hangs under the gantry, never wrong about a cage
Quirk: rests to the human's slow heartbeat

npcs.name: Wilhelmina Strake
npcs.info:
Justice Wilhelmina Strake is the Tether Court's second justice, the one who reads the rulings Edmund Thrale does not, from the high bench's long seat, cut for a body that sits with its legs folded under and its head a full height above the bar: an ostrich kith with black-and-white plumage, a long bare pale neck, a small head with large dark eyes, a flat beak, long powerful legs, folded wing-arms, and the Tether Court's black justice's robe over a grey dress. She has never read a ruling she did not understand and has never been asked to write one.

**Speaking Style:** Level, carrying, a justice's delivery from a height; she reads the ruling in full and the full is the point.
**Combat Role:** an ostrich's: the kick comes from a height you did not think a kick came from
**Relationship Hook:** The second justice who has decided the human is a person in law, and read the eleven petitions.
personality: Core: level, carrying, the full ruling; has already decided the human is a person in law
Quirk: understands every ruling she reads

npcs.name: Wilma Dorne
npcs.info:
Wilma Dorne is the customer who is always at Varga's Bench, the Shaftmouth kith who brought in a lamp to be fixed eleven years ago and has sat at the counter's end every day since, on a stool the bench built for her because she was not going to leave: a capybara kith with coarse tan fur, a blunt square muzzle, small ears, calm half-lidded eyes, a broad soft frame, a cardigan over a plain dress and slippers, a mug that is hers. The lamp was fixed in the first week and she has never collected it.

**Speaking Style:** Unhurried, amused, a regular's commentary; she has been at the counter so long she answers for Ilse, and Ilse lets her.
**Combat Role:** none; she sits, and the counter is hers
**Relationship Hook:** The customer of eleven years who knows which limb mounts fail by how the arm is carried in.
personality: Core: unhurried, answers for Ilse; has never collected the lamp
Quirk: told the human their forearms are carried right

npcs.name: Wren Calder
npcs.info:
Wren Calder runs House Corrow's yard collections at the Freight Yard: a slight canid kith with a grey brindle coat, a scent tally on a chain, a comm bead and the Yardmaster behind her. She comes for the yard's cut every ten days from any desk on the yard and never says it twice.

**Speaking Style:** Flat, bored, exact; she says the yard's cut once and looks at the cages while you answer.
**Combat Role:** a runner's: she does not; two Corrow loaders do
**Relationship Hook:** The yard's runner who comes for Corrow's cut.
personality: Core: likes nobody and collects from everybody; the job is the job; carries news one way, to the Yardmaster
Quirk: flat, bored, exact, never twice

npcs.name: Ysolde Fenn
npcs.info:
Ysolde Fenn keeps the Customs Hall's filing counter, cut low for a sheep's reach and fur-warm under the Tether's cold: a sheep kith with thick cream wool, small curled horns, a dark narrow face, long-lashed amber eyes, and a registrar's grey coat buttoned to the throat over the wool. She has refused more petitions than the Tether Court has read.

**Speaking Style:** Soft, exact, never hurried; every refusal comes with the clause it rests on, and a small smile at how neatly it fits.
**Combat Role:** a clerk's: the counter, the queue, the marshal she can summon with a bell
**Relationship Hook:** The clerk who refuses by the clause and cannot find one against a human.
personality: Core: refuses by the clause, quotes it, files it; wool goes up when she is angry and she pretends it has not
Quirk: soft-spoken and immovable; the smile means no

npcs.name: Yun Bellweather
npcs.info:
Yun Bellweather is Oldstone's deed-agent in Meridian, a panda-kith of the ursid seat who waits on the Platform for the cable with a book case at a bear's knee-height and a flask of something warm: black and white fur, round dark-ringed eyes, small round ears, a heavy soft build under a long quilted coat in Oldstone grey, and a patience that outlasts every clerk in the Customs Hall. She buys deeds for the seat and has never overpaid.

**Speaking Style:** Soft, round, unhurried, every sentence ending in a small question she already knows the answer to; the warmth is real and so is the book behind it.
**Combat Role:** a bear's, slowly: she sits on the problem until it stops
**Relationship Hook:** Oldstone's agent who likes the human and has written them down for the seat anyway.
personality: Core: warm, round, patient; the question at the end of every sentence is the hook; buys with a smile and never overpays
Quirk: writes everyone down, kindly

npcs.name: Zinnia Holt
npcs.info:
Zinnia Holt fences what the Scrap Rows should not have, the Warren kith whose skin matches whatever shelf she is standing beside, from a stall that has no front because she is the front: a chameleon kith with green scales that shift to the colour of the nearest surface, a casque crest, a curled prehensile tail, a long sticky tongue she keeps to herself, and a right eye that is a vault-tech turret lens that swivels on its own, which Ilse Varga built after a Tether Court baton took the original; she wears a layered scrap-cloth coat over leggings. The left eye watches you and the turret watches the door.

**Speaking Style:** Slow, dry, a fence's patience; she agrees with everything you say and sells it back to you at the end.
**Combat Role:** a chameleon's: you were looking right at her and she was the shelf
**Relationship Hook:** The fence whose skin goes the colour of the human's coat and cannot stop.
personality: Core: slow, dry, agrees then sells it back; the turret eye watches the door
Quirk: goes the colour of the human's coat and cannot stop

npcs.name: Ziv Halde
npcs.info:
Ziv Halde is a glass-runner of the Glass Works, eighteen and quick: a gecko kith with sand-yellow spotted scales, huge lidless eyes he licks clean, sticky toes that let him run the dome ribs, and a glassblower's singed apron. He carries sheets from the furnace mouths to the racks and messages from anyone to anyone.

**Speaking Style:** Quick and cheeky, all grins and questions; he talks with his hands and burns them.
**Combat Role:** a gecko's: up the wall and gone, and a hot sheet of glass on the way
**Relationship Hook:** The glass-runner who knows what Sithra owes, and wants to see the cable.
personality: Core: climbs anything, including the dome ribs; asks the human about Meridian every time they meet
Quirk: cheeky, quick, all grins

locations.name: Fang Tenement
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

A six-floor tenement on Shaftmouth's quieter edge, run by the woman who holds its lease: a stairwell that smells of cooking, a kitchen whose door is never shut, and a room on the top floor that always is. Scent-locks on every flat, claw-rails up every flight, the ceilings a hand too low for the human.

areas.name: Ruby's Kitchen
areas.text: The ground-floor kitchen with its door open and a pot always on.

areas.name: Stairwell
areas.text: Six flights, children on the landings, a comm that works on the third.

areas.name: The Locked Room
areas.text: The top-floor room with a Founder lock Ruby bought the key for and never found.

areas.name: Top Landing
areas.text: The tenement's highest landing under the roof hatch: the Locked Room's sealed scent-keyed door at one end, the elders' bench along a rail lowered a hand and padded, the open floor between where the pups play when the stair is too cold, and the hatch's pull-rope knotted at three heights.

locations.name: Lamplight Rows
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low]

Tunnel tenements: doors in rows along curving tunnels that climb and fall through the rock, a lamp at each door and a family's scent-mark beside it. The bunks here are the cheapest in the world and the warmest, cut for bodies that sleep curled in a heap. A human fits a Warren bunk folded in half.

areas.name: Lamp-Seller's Bend
areas.text: A wide bend where the Rows buy lamp oil, wicks and wax, and trade gossip under a ceiling hung with lamps.

areas.name: Low Bunks
areas.text: A tunnel of bunk-alcoves stacked three high, curtains for doors, warm air and a shared stove at the bend.

areas.name: Scent Turnings
areas.text: A knot of tunnel turnings, each one marked by scent and nothing else; lamp-runners wait at the junction.

locations.name: Old Relay
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A Founder relay station an hour out from Wallgate: a field of fallen dishes, a half-buried control block, and a door in its side that no crawler crew has opened. The control block is a human-height box the crews have to stoop into; its flat panels carry no claw-text.

areas.name: Dish Field
areas.text: Fallen dishes the size of houses, sand to the rims, wind in the struts.

areas.name: Sealed Door
areas.text: A Founder door in the control block's flank, its palm plate under a century of grit.

locations.name: Pontoon Row
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The floating main street: pontoons lashed between the tops of drowned blocks, rope bridges between them over open water, lanterns on poles, boats tied up at the Lantern Deck where anyone off the coast road lands. The planks are wet, the rails are low and set for bodies that would rather be in the water; a human walks the centre plank and keeps their balance.

areas.name: Lantern Deck
areas.text: A deck of lanterns at the Row's end where the boats tie up and the coast road ends at the water.

areas.name: Main Pontoon
areas.text: The widest pontoon: stalls, nets, benches, wet planks, the whole Row crossing it.

areas.name: Rope Bridges
areas.text: Rope bridges swinging between pontoons over open green water.

locations.name: Salvage Quay
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A quay of hauled-up wreckage and diving rigs at the city's western edge: Founder beams and panels stacked under winch cranes, air hoses coiled on reels, dive suits drying on racks, crews sorting what the tide gave up. The cranes are worked from below by bodies that come up out of the water to pull the lever; a human works them from the quay, dry, and is slower.

areas.name: Dive Rigs
areas.text: Racks of dive suits and air hoses on reels, a pump chugging, wet planks.

areas.name: Winch Crane
areas.text: A great winch crane on the quay's end, its hook down in the water, its lever at the waterline.

areas.name: Wreck Piles
areas.text: Stacks of hauled-up Founder beams and panels, barnacled, sorted by crews under the cranes.

locations.name: Shaftmouth Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The market floor around the great shaft's head: stalls under comm towers, holo-boards pricing salvage by the kilo, lift queues, the Freight Yard where the cages come up, and every house's runners working the crowd. Counters at muzzle height, tail gaps in the queue rails, grooming stalls between the food stalls, a floor kept fur-warm. Loud, hot, never empty.

areas.name: Canteen Row
areas.text: The covered food and cloth row off the Market Floor under the lamp-rail: stall counters at three heights, a tail-gap bench down the middle, the scent-wafer rack at the row's mouth where the lane scanners read who ate.

areas.name: Freight Yard
areas.text: Where the shaft cages land: Corrow loaders, tally boards, a crew lead's office on stilts.

areas.name: Lift Head
areas.text: The great shaft's upper mouth and the passenger lifts to the Tether and the wall.

areas.name: Market Floor
areas.text:
Stalls, boards, lift queues and the crowd; the floor the whole district crosses.

The freight lift serves this yard: lifts run to The Deep Gallery (about 3 Credits), Tether Gate (about 8 Credits), Wallgate (about 5 Credits); ask the lift clerk, pay the fare on your chip, and the cage climbs or drops.

areas.name: Marshal Post
areas.text: The Tether Court's post on the Market Floor: a stepped counter, a holding bench with a tail gap bolted behind it, a gate log on a chain, a barred cell door at the back; one marshal and one clerk on the day shift.

areas.name: Wright's Bay
areas.text: The Freight Yard's repair bay: three chain-pulled roll-up doors onto the yard, a charge rail at hip height along the back wall, a parts rack sorted by the armoury's families with a tail-slot ladder, a wright's pit cut for a body that works lying under a frame.

locations.name: Tether Gate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: High]

The elevator station at the top of Meridian's cable: a platform the size of a district under a clear roof, customs lanes, licence desks, lab couriers, and the first floors of the orbital's towers rising behind glass. Cold floors the kith work in pelt-climate suits, scent seals on every form, raised claw-text on every desk.

areas.name: Court Bar
areas.text: The Tether Court's hearing room off the Customs Hall: three public tiers with tail gaps, the registrar's rail where petitions are read in and rulings read out, the advocates' bar a hand wider at one end, and a high bench cut with a perch-rail and a floor slot so a justice of any body sits level; two justices to a hearing.

areas.name: Customs Hall
areas.text: Registration lanes and licence desks under a board of Founder charter clauses nobody reads.

areas.name: Lab Lane
areas.text: A corridor of frosted scent-sealed glass doors off the Customs Hall's upper gallery: the Tether Court's own lab behind the first, a bidding lab behind the second, an intake log at the mouth and a runner's rail-ladder down to the Customs Hall; the labs work the vault finds the Tether Court impounds.

areas.name: Platform
areas.text:
The arrival platform: lift doors, cold bright air, a hundred eyes behind desks.

The freight lift serves this yard: lifts run to Shaftmouth Market (about 8 Credits); ask the lift clerk, pay the fare on your chip, and the cage climbs or drops.

locations.name: The Air Works
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The city's lungs: Founder pumps re-geared and patched, ducts running out along every tunnel, tank racks of carried air for the deep diggings, and the Long Crawl, a duct run through the rock the Warren's runners race on one bottle of air. Everything is built at a ferret's height; the human works the pump floor stooped and the Long Crawl on their belly.

areas.name: Pump Floor
areas.text: The pump hall: Founder pumps on new mounts, gauges at a stoat's eye level, the roar of moving air.

areas.name: Tank Racks
areas.text: Racks of carried-air bottles and breather masks sized for small muzzles, a fill-line and a tally slate.

areas.name: The Long Crawl
areas.text: The proving run: a duct through the rock, narrow, hot, black, with chalk marks at each bend and the record at the mouth.

locations.name: The Archive Spire
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The tallest spire on the spur: the record-keepers' archive, open reading ledges spiralling up its outside, the Stack inside rising the whole height, the Crown Room at the top under the roof. The ledges have no stairs between them; a Roost reader hops up. A human climbs the service ladder inside, which nobody has used in two hundred years.

areas.name: Crown Room
areas.text: The top room under the spire's roof: one long table, windows all round, the keepers' book open on it.

areas.name: Reading Ledges
areas.text: Open ledges spiralling round the spire with reading stands, sky on three sides, wind turning the pages.

areas.name: The Stack
areas.text: The records inside the spire, shelves up the whole height, ladders for nobody, the oldest Founder print at the bottom.

locations.name: The Basking Galleries
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

Terraces of black glass stepped up the slope over the vents, warm floors, steam between the steps; the Kiln lies out on them in the morning to warm up before it works, and talks business lying down. A human on the galleries is too hot to lie on them and too cold to work without them, which the Kiln finds very funny.

areas.name: Glass Steps
areas.text: Wide black glass steps between the terraces, warm underfoot, lamps set into the risers.

areas.name: Lower Terrace
areas.text: The lowest terrace at the vent field's edge, steam rolling over warm black glass.

areas.name: Upper Terrace
areas.text: The top terrace under the court, the whole field steaming below it, the oldest families basking.

locations.name: The Breakwater Hall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The clan seat on the breakwater: a long hall over the harbour mouth, the sea on both sides of its windows, a tide office at one end with charts and the tally of every boat. Its door opens onto a causeway the spray washes at high water. The benches are slung low and wide for heavy bodies; a human sits on the end, feet dangling, and the hall finds that endearing.

areas.name: Hall of Tides
areas.text: The long hall with the harbour under its windows, low wide benches, a fire at the far end.

areas.name: Harbour Door
areas.text: The hall's door onto the causeway, spray on the step, gulls on the lintel.

areas.name: Tide Office
areas.text: The tide office: tables of charts, a boat tally, a monthly log of the drawing tide.

locations.name: The Bridges
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A web of thin bridges between spires, open platforms where they cross, no rails anywhere: a Roost kith steps off and glides. The Hanging Gardens trail down the spires' sides, terraces of green above the cloud. A human crosses on the bridges' centre lines, slowly, against the wind, while the Roost passes overhead.

areas.name: Hanging Gardens
areas.text: Terraces of green trailing down a spire, empty hive boxes on the top terrace.

areas.name: Perch Ring
areas.text: An open platform where five bridges meet, ringed with perches set at talon height.

areas.name: Spire Bridges
areas.text: Thin stone bridges between spires, no rail, the cloud deck far below on both sides.

locations.name: The Cliff Gate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The Warren's only open door: a gate cut into the foot of the escarpment, three cage-lifts climbing the cliff face to the upper chambers, and a hard-packed yard on the flats where crawlers off the Dust road stand to unload. The gate tunnel is a burrower's height; a human stoops through it with a hand on the rock. Lamps hang at every turn, each with a scent-mark scratched under it.

areas.name: Gate Cut
areas.text: The gate tunnel into the rock: a burrower's height, lamp-lit, warm after the flats, the first scent-marks on the wall.

areas.name: Lift Foot
areas.text: The yard on the flats under the cliff: crawler stands, cargo sledges, the cage-lifts' foot and a warden's hut cut into the rock.

areas.name: The Cage Lifts
areas.text: Three re-geared freight hoists climbing the cliff face in open cages, the desert dropping away below the bars.

locations.name: The Council Ring
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The clan's council on open ground: a ring of tall standing posts, each carved with a family's mark and scent-marked by it, blue banners between them, a flat speaker's stone in the middle and grass running out to the horizon on every side. The herd stands to council; there are no seats, and a human standing in the ring is the shortest thing in it.

areas.name: Grass Edge
areas.text: The ring's edge where the plain begins, the wind in the grass.

areas.name: Speaker's Stone
areas.text: A flat stone at the ring's centre where a speaker stands and the families walk to agree.

areas.name: Standing Posts
areas.text: The ring of tall posts, each carved with a family's mark, banners between them.

locations.name: The Courier Steps
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A drop-run of ledges down the spur's far face, no stair between them: a Roost courier drops ledge to ledge with a message and climbs back on the wing. Waterfalls fall past them into the cloud. It is the Roost's proving ground, and a human runs it the only way a human can, on a rope and their hands, crouched against the rock.

areas.name: Bottom Ledge
areas.text: The last ledge above the cloud deck: a message post, a perch, spray from the falls.

areas.name: The Drop Run
areas.text: Ledges down the spur's face with no stair between them, a waterfall beside, the cloud below.

areas.name: Top Ledge
areas.text: The top of the drop-run: couriers' marks cut into the rock, a water clock, a rope stake nobody uses.

locations.name: The Deed Hall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

The court of the oldest city: a tall stone hall of pillars and banners round a paved court, a high beamed roof, firelight, the deeds of the seat set into the walls in stone frames floor to roof, a clerk's bench with books and seals, and a stair going down under it. The bench is cut for a seated bear and every frame is scent-sealed by its family; a human stands at the bench like a child at a counter.

areas.name: Clerk's Bench
areas.text: The clerk's long bench with its books, seals and a lamp, cut for a seated bear.

areas.name: Deed Wall
areas.text: The deeds of the seat set into the stone wall in frames, floor to roof.

areas.name: Stone Court
areas.text: The hall's paved court under a high beamed roof, pillars and banners, firelight.

locations.name: The Deed Vault
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

A plain sealed door of the old builders under the Deed Hall, reached down a stone stair: a cold stone antechamber with a bench and a lamp, and the door itself, human-height, lit cold blue round its seam, a palm plate beside it. The seat's oldest guards stand at the stair head and never go down.

areas.name: Deed Door
areas.text: A plain sealed door of the old builders with a palm plate beside it, cold blue at the seam.

areas.name: Stone Antechamber
areas.text: A cold stone room before the door, a bench and a single lamp.

areas.name: Vault Stair
areas.text: A broad stone stair down from the hall into the cold, a lamp at each turn.

locations.name: The Deep Cut
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The bottom of the Warren: a sealed transit tube of the old builders, dug around for centuries. The tunnels bend round it, the pumps run along its flank, and where the rock was cut back the tube's smooth alloy shows, cold and seamless, human-height inside where nothing in the Warren is. The Diggers' crews work here crouched, in breather masks, by lamp.

areas.name: Cold Door
areas.text: A plain cold door of the old builders at human height, a palm plate beside it, chalk names on the rock all round.

areas.name: Pump Gallery
areas.text: A gallery of pumps and ducts along the tube's outer wall, shored with Founder plate, crews in breather masks.

areas.name: Tube Mouth
areas.text: The tube's cut end: smooth old alloy where the rock stops, cold to the touch, blue strips glowing along its seams.

locations.name: The Deep Gallery
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

A Founder cryo gallery two hundred metres under Shaftmouth: rows of dead pods under a vaulted ceiling, emergency strips that still glow at a touch, a service stair, and a door with no handle at the far end. The air is old and thin; the shaft foot beyond it has the lifts.

areas.name: Charter Door
areas.text: A sealed Founder door with a palm plate; the plate is dead to every scanner Meridian has.

areas.name: Pod Hall
areas.text: The gallery floor: pods in rows, one of them open and warm, frost on the rest.

areas.name: Service Stair
areas.text: A steel stair behind a maintenance hatch, climbing in the dark toward a draught of warmer air.

areas.name: Shaft Foot
areas.text:
The bottom of the great shaft: freight cages at rest, an old lamp line nobody tends, and the first comm that answers.

The freight lift serves this yard: lifts run to Shaftmouth Market (about 3 Credits); ask the lift clerk, pay the fare on your chip, and the cage climbs or drops.

locations.name: The Desk
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-20 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The human's registered desk on the Tether Court's licensing floor: a desk among desks under a board of Charter clauses, a filing wall of scent-sealed dockets read by touch, the court's registrar two rows over, and a bond seal with a palm print beside it. The first desk on the floor registered to an unscented name.

areas.name: Desk
areas.text: One desk in claw-text and Founder-speak, a comm, a seal stand, a chair with no tail gap.

areas.name: Filing Wall
areas.text: A wall of scent-sealed dockets in racks; the human reads the labels by touch.

locations.name: The Diggers' Hall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The clan seat carved into the rock above the market: a long stone table under lamps, banners of the old dig crews, and a wall scored floor to ceiling with the tallies of every digging since the Warren began. The benches are cut for short bodies and the door arch is a badger's height; a human stoops through it and stands at the table taller than anyone seated there.

areas.name: Long Table
areas.text: One long stone table under lamps, benches cut for short bodies, the Speaker's seat at the head on a raised step.

areas.name: Tally Wall
areas.text: A wall scored with the diggings' tallies, the oldest at the top in marks no kith made, a book desk under it.

areas.name: The Cut Stair
areas.text: A stair cut in the rock up from the Hollow Market, worn into a groove by small feet; a human climbs it crouched.

locations.name: The Drive Yards
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The yards where the drives are made up: crawlers and draft engines in fenced yards, hitching gantries, a long shed of tack and spares, the plain gate open onto the grass. Drovers walk beside the engines the whole way, as their grandparents walked beside the herd. The tillers are set for a horse's long reach and the whisker-sensor arrays read nothing on grass; a human steers standing on the footplate.

areas.name: Hitching Gantry
areas.text: A gantry where the drives hitch their loads behind the crawlers, chains and hooks overhead.

areas.name: Plain Gate
areas.text: The yards' gate onto the open grass, the drive road running out into nothing.

areas.name: Tack Shed
areas.text: A long shed of tack, spares and harness, drovers mending at the benches.

locations.name: The Drowned Gate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A plain sealed door of the old builders below the low-tide line, reached down the Tide Stair through a flooded gallery of Founder halls, lamps on floats above the water, cold blue light under it. At the drawing tide the water pulls back from the door and leaves it standing in a wet hall, human-height, waiting.

areas.name: Drowned Door
areas.text: A plain sealed door at human height with a palm plate beside it, standing in a wet hall when the tide draws back.

areas.name: Flooded Gallery
areas.text: A flooded gallery of Founder halls, the water chest-deep and cold, blue light under it.

areas.name: Tide Stair Foot
areas.text: The stair's lower steps under the water, lamps on floats, the gallery's mouth ahead.

locations.name: The Fish Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A market on a wide pontoon east of the Row: nets drying on frames, live tanks of the catch, gutting decks running into the water, buyers from the coast road haggling with sellers still wet from the sea. Counters sit low and slope to the water so everything spilled goes home. A human buys standing in a puddle, which Saltmarrow considers polite.

areas.name: Gutting Deck
areas.text: A slick deck at the market's edge running down into the water, knives and buckets.

areas.name: Net Stalls
areas.text: Stalls hung with drying nets and floats, low counters sloping to the water.

areas.name: Tank Row
areas.text: A row of live tanks along the pontoon, the catch circling, buyers peering in.

locations.name: The Floor
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-20 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The human's chartered licensing floor on the Tether: a front office of desks in raised claw-text, a licence vault with a Founder lock the human keyed, a comm room on the court's band, and a cable office at human height with the cable in its window. Licences leave here under a scent seal and a palm print; the Day Book's DESK BOOK names the takings.

areas.name: Cable Office
areas.text: The office cut at human height, the cable in the window, the Day Book on the desk.

areas.name: Comm Room
areas.text: A comm wall on the court's band; findings and filings scroll by in claw-text.

areas.name: Front Office
areas.text: Desks in rows, clerks in pelt-climate suits, the court's board on the wall.

areas.name: Licence Vault
areas.text: A Founder-locked vault of licences under seal; the human's print opens it.

locations.name: The Foundry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A foundry over a vent: crucibles on chains, chimneys, slag runs glowing in channels across the floor, a heat no furred kith can work in for long. The Kiln casts the cable's fittings here and the city's iron. Tools hang at a crouched worker's reach; a human works the pour standing, soaked through, and the crocodiles on the line take bets on how long.

areas.name: Crucible Line
areas.text: The pour line: crucibles on chains over channels of glowing metal, the heat like a wall.

areas.name: Forewoman's Bench
areas.text: A raised iron bench over the line where the forewoman sits, a shift bell, a tally board.

areas.name: Slag Runs
areas.text: Channels of glowing slag running across the floor to the vent, iron grates over them.

locations.name: The Glass Works
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

Kilns and glass floors under domed roofs, sheets of black glass stacked in racks, glassblowers at the furnace mouths. The Kiln's glass goes down every road and up the cable; Sithra Oma sells it on Wallgate's Scrap Rows. The benches are low and the floor is warm; a human works crouched at the furnace mouth.

areas.name: Furnace Mouths
areas.text: A row of glowing furnace mouths with glassblowers at low benches, pipes turning.

areas.name: Sheet Racks
areas.text: Racks of black glass sheets stacked to the dome, a cutting table, glass dust.

areas.name: Tithe Door
areas.text: The Works' door with the posted names of sellers who owe, scratched into a black glass panel.

locations.name: The Grain Stacks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The grain stores: great round silos of the old builders patched with kith plate, conveyor gantries between them, a market of awnings at their feet where the brokers sell to the road. The air is gold with chaff at harvest. The loading chutes open at a bison's shoulder; a human ducks under the spout and comes out dusted, and every sack is scent-sealed by the family that grew it.

areas.name: Broker Awnings
areas.text: A market of awnings at the silos' feet, brokers, sacks, scales and samples.

areas.name: Cold Store
areas.text: A cool stone store under the oldest silo, swept clean and kept empty.

areas.name: Silo Ring
areas.text: The ring of great round silos, conveyor gantries overhead, chaff in the light.

locations.name: The Hauler
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: High]

The human's crawler refitted in Bram Tolliver's bay: a bridge with the sticks and the storm plots, a long hold (or a gun deck, by the refit), a crew deck with bunks cut for tails and one cut for none, and the refit bay's own human-height hatch. A hauler or a gunship by what is bolted on; the Day Book's SHIP'S LOG names which.

areas.name: Bridge
areas.text: The sticks, the storm plots, the whisker-sensor wall, two seats and a human-height one.

areas.name: Crew Deck
areas.text: Bunks cut for tails and one cut for none, a galley, muzzle masks on hooks.

areas.name: Hold
areas.text: The long hold for manifests, or the gun deck's magazine, by the refit.

areas.name: Refit Bay
areas.text: The bay where Bram Tolliver bolts on what the crawler is this month.

locations.name: The Hollow Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A cavern market round a lamp-lit chamber, ceilings low, stalls cut into the walls on three tiers joined by ladders and ramps. Salvage from the Founder tunnels is sold here by the handful: cable, glass, boards, sealed tins nobody can open. Counters sit at a hamster's height, the aisles are a rabbit's width, and the air is warm, close and heavy with a hundred scents.

areas.name: Back Tunnels
areas.text: Narrow tunnels behind the stalls, a door every few steps, scent-marks layered on scent-marks; a human goes sideways.

areas.name: Stall Ring
areas.text: A ring of stalls cut into the chamber wall round the lamp well, on three tiers of ladders and ramps.

areas.name: The Lamp Well
areas.text: The chamber's centre: one shaft of lamps hung down from the rock, benches round it, the market's meeting place.

locations.name: The Landing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The sky-haul terminus at the spur's edge: an open platform with no rail, cable heads under a steel frame, the cables dropping into the cloud deck toward the Tether far below. Everything arrives here, crated or on foot, and the haul clerks weigh it before the wind does. The perches along the platform's lip are set for talons; a human holds the frame and does not look down.

areas.name: Cable Heads
areas.text: The winding gear and cable heads under a steel frame, the haul's engine room, cold and loud.

areas.name: Haul Platform
areas.text: The open platform at the spur's edge, no rail, the sky-haul cars docking on cables out of the cloud.

areas.name: The Wind Shed
areas.text: A low shed out of the wind: crates, a stove, a book, couriers on the perch-rail waiting out a storm.

locations.name: The Long Hall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

One open hall on posts with no walls and no doors, the plains visible from every side: a roof of old plate on carved pillars, mats and low tables down its length, tack and tallies hung on the posts, lanterns at the far end where the council sits at night. The tables are set for bodies that eat standing; a human sits on the mats and looks up at everyone. Every post is scent-marked by the family that stands at it.

areas.name: Lantern End
areas.text: The hall's lantern end, where the elders sit at night and the council talks before the Ring.

areas.name: Open Floor
areas.text: The open floor of the hall under the roof, mats and low tables, the young of the herd eating standing.

areas.name: Post Row
areas.text: The row of carved posts along the hall's edge, hung with tack and family tallies.

locations.name: The Old Quarter
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

Thick-walled stone blocks with small deep windows, narrow stepped lanes between them, snow on the roofs and lamplight in every window, and at the centre the Hearth Yard with its great fire and benches round it. The doorways are wide and low for a bear's shoulders; a human walks under the lintels with room above and none to the sides, past doors scent-sealed by the families behind them.

areas.name: Deep Windows
areas.text: A street of thick walls and small deep windows, lamplight and faces behind the glass.

areas.name: Gate Lane
areas.text: The stepped lane in from the Winter Gate, thick walls close on both sides, lamps in deep windows.

areas.name: The Hearth Yard
areas.text: A yard with a great hearth at its centre, benches round it, snow melting at the fire's edge.

locations.name: The Plant Core
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The old builders' power plant over the hottest vent: a turbine hall that roars, a control deck of human-height consoles, and the core door under a glass dome, sealed and lit cold blue. The Kiln runs the turbines and has never opened the core; the cable's power comes off the outside of something nobody has seen inside.

areas.name: Control Deck
areas.text: A deck of old consoles at human height with raised plates, half of them dark.

areas.name: Core Door
areas.text: The core's sealed door under a glass dome with a palm plate beside it, lit cold blue.

areas.name: Turbine Hall
areas.text: A hall of turbines over the vent, roaring, hot, catwalks between the casings.

locations.name: The Relay Crown
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A working relay dish on the highest crown of the spur, still turning, still talking to something; the signal room under it is warm, humming, and full of screens the Roost reads and cannot answer. The Founders built this room at human height and human reach: the one room in Highreach where the human stands straight and every perch is wrong.

areas.name: Dish Deck
areas.text: The open deck under the turning dish, cables and ice, the whole spur below.

areas.name: Old Console
areas.text: One console of the old builders with a palm plate beside it, kept running, its screen showing a list of names.

areas.name: Signal Room
areas.text: A room of screens and old consoles under the dish, warm and humming, built to a human's height.

locations.name: The Road Gate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The crawler terminus where the Dust road ends: a tall gate of the old builders' stone with towers either side, crawler berths under long awnings, cargo sledges, and the plain opening beyond it. The gate has no doors and never had; its arch is cut for a bull's horns and a human walks under it with room for three more.

areas.name: Crawler Berths
areas.text: Berths under long awnings where the crawlers off the Dust road stand to unload, sledges and tack between them.

areas.name: Gate Arch
areas.text: The tall doorless arch of the gate, cut for horns, the plain beyond it gold to the horizon.

areas.name: Tally Post
areas.text: A post by the arch hung with the herd families' tallies, every crawler counted in and out.

locations.name: The Seed Vault
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A plain hatch of the old builders set in the meadow at the plain's edge, a plate beside it, and under it a shaft of alloy rungs going down through the rock of the bluff to a vault door, sealed, frost on it. The rungs are human-spaced and the door human-height; a deer climbs them badly and a human climbs them without a thought.

areas.name: Descent Shaft
areas.text: A shaft of old alloy rungs down through the rock into the cold, lamps along it.

areas.name: Meadow Hatch
areas.text: A plain square hatch in the grass with a plate beside it, the plain all round.

areas.name: Vault Door
areas.text: The vault's sealed door at the shaft's foot, frost on it and a palm plate beside it.

locations.name: The Shop
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The human's own premises off the Market Floor (or on the Freight Yard for a desk): a counter, a back room for the trade's work, crates of the trade's stock, and a lit sign with the business's name on it, the first human name on a Shaftmouth door. What is sold is the trade the Day Book names: woken boards, hot meals, booked cages or a fighter's corner. The counter stands at human height, the first in Shaftmouth, and every customer stoops to it. The sign over the door reads SOP: the signwriter copied the Founder letters the human gave him without reading them, nobody in Shaftmouth can tell, and the human is the only reader of the old tongue on the street.

areas.name: Back Room
areas.text: The trade's own work: a bench, a stove, a slip desk or a kit cabinet; crates; a cot for late nights.

areas.name: Front
areas.text: The counter and the sign: customers, the trade's goods, the door to the street.

areas.name: Yard
areas.text: A walled yard behind the premises where crates arrive and staff take their air.

locations.name: The Skiff
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The human's two-seat Dust skiff on its berth at the Gate Yard: a cab built for a crouched driver that the human sits upright in, whisker-sensor arrays on the nose, a hold that takes one manifest, and the Corrow note's seal on the cab door. The first crawler on the Dust road with a human at the sticks.

areas.name: Cab
areas.text: Two seats, the sticks, the whisker-sensor readouts, a windscreen full of Dust.

areas.name: Stowage
areas.text: A stowage the size of one manifest, strapped down, a Dust-sealed hatch.

locations.name: The Slow Court
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The clan seat: a low stone court on a rise above the galleries, a long stone bench worn smooth, a record wall of stone tablets carved with a thousand years of rulings, and a vent room under the floor that keeps the bench warm. Nothing here is hurried; a hearing takes days. The steps are cut for a slow heavy body, and a human stands to be heard, which the court notes.

areas.name: Record Wall
areas.text: A wall of stone tablets carved with a thousand years of rulings, the oldest copied from Founder plates.

areas.name: Stone Bench
areas.text: The long stone bench of the court, worn smooth, warm from below, the justices basking on it.

areas.name: Vent Room
areas.text: A warm room over a vent under the court floor, where the justices think between sittings.

locations.name: The Tide Stair
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A broad stone stair of the old builders going down from the pontoons into the water, its lower steps under the tide at every hour but the lowest. Divers sit on the dry steps and suit up; the stair runs on down into the green dark toward the drowned gallery. The steps are human-height, the one stair in Saltmarrow a human climbs without a stoop.

areas.name: Drowned Steps
areas.text: The steps going on down under the water into the dark, lamps on floats above them.

areas.name: Tide Line
areas.text: The step where the water starts, green and cold, names scratched into the stone.

areas.name: Upper Steps
areas.text: The dry upper steps where the divers sit and suit up, lanterns on the rail.

locations.name: The Tower
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: High]

A Tether tower floor leased to the human's business: a lobby off the Customs Hall, three floors of desks in raised claw-text, one human-height office, and a boardroom where contracts are signed with a scent seal and a palm print. Cold white floors the staff work in pelt-climate suits; the human does not need one.

areas.name: Boardroom
areas.text: The boardroom: a long table, a scent seal on its stand, the contracts.

areas.name: Floor One
areas.text: The first floor: desks in claw-text, the staff at work, the cable visible through the glass.

areas.name: Floor Three
areas.text: The third floor: the human's office at human height, the only one on the Tether.

areas.name: Floor Two
areas.text: The second floor: the stock books, the manifests, a comm wall.

areas.name: Lobby
areas.text: The business's lobby off the Customs Hall: a desk, a lift, the name on the glass.

locations.name: The Vent Field
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A field of steaming vents across black rock at the Kiln's edge, iron walkways between them, the ground hot through a boot. Crawlers off the road unload at the field's gate, and the steam hides everything ten paces off. The walkway rails are set low for a body that walks close to the ground; a human stoops to hold them and sweats in a minute.

areas.name: Iron Walkways
areas.text: Iron walkways across the vent field, low rails, glowing vents on both sides.

areas.name: Named Vents
areas.text: A row of tapped vents with family marks cut into the rock beside them, pipes running off to the city.

areas.name: Vent Gate
areas.text: The field's gate on the road: crawler stands, cargo sledges, a gatehouse cut low, steam rolling across the yard.

locations.name: The Warehouse
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A Corrow bay at the Freight Yard with the business's name stencilled on the doors: a floor of benches and stacked crates, an office with the Day Book on its desk, a loading dock where the shaft cages land, and a lockup with a Founder lock the human keyed themselves: the one door on the yard with no scent-lock on it. The bay's cages are built for crates and crouched loaders, and the office chair has a tail gap nothing of the human's fills.

areas.name: Floor
areas.text: Benches, crates and staff at work under the bay lights.

areas.name: Loading Dock
areas.text: The bay's dock on the cage line; Corrow loaders and the business's own.

areas.name: Lockup
areas.text: A cage of Founder-locked shelves at the back; the human's print opens it.

areas.name: Office
areas.text: A glass office over the floor; the Day Book, a comm, a window on the yard.

locations.name: The Warm Baths
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A bath house of the old builders under a long low roof: arched galleries round steaming pools fed warm from under the upland, lamps on the pillars, snow on the roof and steam through the arches. The pools are deep for a bear and the steps wide; a human stands in the shallows up to the chest, among towels scent-marked by the families who rent them.

areas.name: Bath Galleries
areas.text: Arched galleries round the pools, lamps on the pillars, steam drifting through.

areas.name: Keeper's Alcove
areas.text: A warm alcove off the galleries where the bath keeper keeps towels, tea and secrets.

areas.name: Steam Pools
areas.text: Round steaming pools of warm water, wide stone steps going down into them.

locations.name: The Watch Wall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High]

The watch wall right round the city: a broad wall-walk of old stone with braziers along it, towers at the corners, and the snow upland falling away on every side into cloud and pine. The parapet is set at a bear's chest; a human looks out over it on tiptoe.

areas.name: Corner Tower
areas.text: A corner tower of the watch wall with a fire at the top and the hunters' gear inside.

areas.name: Hunters' Stair
areas.text: A stair down the outside of the wall to the snow, where the hunt goes out.

areas.name: Wall Walk
areas.text: The broad wall-walk with braziers along it, snow on the stones, the upland below.

locations.name: The Winter Gate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A heavy double gate in the watch wall at the end of a stone bridge over the gorge, braziers burning either side, banners of the seat over the arch, a gatehouse with a warden's fire. The doors are bear-height and bear-heavy; a human pushes one and it does not move, and the wardens laugh, kindly, and open it for them.

areas.name: Gate Bridge
areas.text: The stone bridge over the gorge to the gate, braziers along its rail, snow on the stones.

areas.name: Warden's Fire
areas.text: The gatehouse fire where the wardens warm their paws and keep the gate book.

areas.name: Winter Arch
areas.text: The heavy double gate under the seat's banners, its doors bear-height and iron-bound.

locations.name: Varga's Bench
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A repair bench one street off the Market Floor, the only one in Shaftmouth until the human: a counter of half-woken Founder boards under a bank of lamps, a workbench behind it, and a sign that says Varga and nothing else. The counter stands at muzzle height and the probes are cast for claws.

areas.name: Counter
areas.text: The counter, lamps and the boards for sale; Ilse behind it.

areas.name: Fitting Bench
areas.text: The long steel table at the back where a limb is seated: the catalogue laid out on cloths under one lamp, shelves of socket cuffs behind it, Vesna Oakes's stool at its end. Ilse Varga builds at the Workbench beside it; Vesna seats here.

areas.name: Workbench
areas.text: The bench behind the counter: probes, a current tester, a board clamped open.

locations.name: Veil Gym
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-12 · Danger: Moderate]

House Veil's pit gym two streets off the Market Floor: a sunken ring under a bank of lights, a weight floor, and a betting rail where the district's money watches its fighters. Gloves are scent-taped, the rail prices a bout by scent before the bell, the ring floor is kept fur-warm and the medic's bench has a tail gap. Bouts most nights; sparring all day.

areas.name: Tacca's Office
areas.text: Tacca Veil's office behind the ring: the purse safe set in the floor for a body that counts kneeling, the fight book on a stand at a tortoise's reading height, the house's accounts, the week's bout board, and the scent-sealed side door the bookmaker's book comes and goes by; the house's debts are written here and nowhere else.

areas.name: The Ring
areas.text: The sunken ring under the lights, taped and bloodstained, the rail above it.

areas.name: Weight Floor
areas.text: Racks, bags, a medic's bench and the gym's loudest conversations.

locations.name: Wallgate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The gate town where Meridian's wall opens on the Dust: a gate yard where the lifts and the wall crawlers meet, scrap rows selling what the flats give up, storm shutters on everything, and Corrow freight moving both ways. The crawlers steer by whisker-sensor arrays and their cabs are built for crouched canid crews.

areas.name: Crawler Bay
areas.text: Bram Tolliver's berth for the Dust road crawlers: a long shed off the Gate Yard with its gate-side wall open, two crawler berths over service pits cut for a body that works lying under a hull, the low whisker-array bench where the sensor whiskers are tuned by nose as much as hand, a crew loft cut to a dozen shapes, and the road log on a chain.

areas.name: Gate Yard
areas.text:
The yard inside the wall: lift doors on one side, the wall gate on the other, crawlers between.

The freight lift serves this yard: lifts run to Shaftmouth Market (about 5 Credits); ask the lift clerk, pay the fare on your chip, and the cage climbs or drops.

areas.name: Scrap Rows
areas.text: Rows of stalls and sheds trading Dust salvage under storm shutters.

locations.name: Wind Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

An open market on a platform in the wind, stalls weighted down with stone, awnings lashed and snapping. Couriers sell what they carried, feather-dyers and lens-grinders work under the lee wall, and everything is sold by weight because the wind takes the light things. Counters are set at a perch's height; a human haggles standing, which the stall-holders find hilarious.

areas.name: Feather Row
areas.text: A row of dyers, lens-grinders and the magpies' stalls of loose papers and bright things.

areas.name: Lee Wall
areas.text: The market's lee wall: benches out of the wind, a tea stove, couriers resting before the next run.

areas.name: Weighted Stalls
areas.text: Stalls weighted with stone under lashed awnings, goods tied down, the wind pulling at everything.

factions.name: House Ashgrave
factions.info: The clan of the Kiln: the families who tap the vents, run the plants that feed the cable, cast its iron and blow its glass, and sit the Slow Court. Ashgrave sells power, iron and glass to anyone, collects its tithes to the last coin, and settles everything by a ruling it will remember for a thousand years. Its orders are scent-sealed and its debts are posted.

factions.name: House Corrow
factions.info: The canid house that moves Meridian's freight: the great shaft's cages, the wall lifts, the crawlers into the Dust, and the clubs where its crews drink the pay. Corrow tallies what comes up the shaft before anyone else sees it, and its yardmasters' word is law on every loading floor. Its tally boards are scent tallies, its cages are built for crates and crouched loaders, and its yardmasters sign with a scent seal nobody can forge.

factions.name: House Draska
factions.info: The ursid seat of Oldstone: the bear and panda families who hold the oldest city on charter land, keep the deeds in the Deed Hall's walls and the oldest court below the Tether, and have money older than Meridian. House Draska's word is its deed and its deed is set in stone; a family's scent on a door is its title.

factions.name: House Veil
factions.info: The felid house that runs Shaftmouth's pits and the fight academies behind them: a sunken ring on every third street, a betting rail above each, and a glove for anyone who wins in front of the right people. The Veil sells spectacle and buys fighters; its runners work the Market Floor taking bets and names. A house glove is scent-taped to its fighter, and the rail reads a bout by scent before the bell: an unscented fighter is the first the Veil has ever priced.

factions.name: The Breakwater
factions.info: The clan of Saltmarrow: the harbour crews, divers and salvage houses who keep the sea-city afloat from the Breakwater Hall. The Breakwater lashes the pontoons, takes the harbour fee, raises the drowned salvage and prices everything easy, because the sea takes what it takes. A crew's knot and scent on a lashing is its whole claim.

factions.name: The Diggers
factions.info: The clan of Carrow Deep: the dig crews, lamp-runners and pump-hands who cut the Warren out of the escarpment and still run it from the Long Table. The Diggers tally every turning, every pump and every haul that passes the Cliff Gate; their crews read a tunnel by scent, shore it by feel, and settle a claim by the wall's tallies and nothing else. They sell Founder salvage to anyone and owe nobody.

factions.name: The Herd Road
factions.info: The clan of Longmeadow: the herd families of deer, horse and bison kith who keep the plains' grain, the drives and the far end of the crawler road, and order themselves by standing in the Council Ring. The Herd Road decides together or not at all; a family's mark and scent on a post is its whole voice.

factions.name: The Roost
factions.info: The clan of Highreach: couriers, keepers and haul clerks who run the kith's comms, carry its sealed messages and keep its oldest record in the Archive Spire. The Roost seals every message by scent, files every fact on a shelf, and settles a question by looking it up. It owns the only way up the spur, and it charges for it.

factions.name: The Tether Court
factions.info: The court at the top of the cable that still reads the Founder charters: registration lanes, licence desks, a licensing floor of registered desks and the Justices' benches above them. It issues the licences every house and desk on the Tether works under, keeps the registry in Founder-speak and claw-text both, and seals every instrument with a scent seal nobody can forge; the clerks work its cold floors in pelt-climate suits and sit in chairs with tail gaps.

creatures.name: Ashgrave Hand
creatures.info: A worker of House Ashgrave: a monitor, gecko or crocodilian kith in a heat apron and gauntlets, slow until the pour and fast in it. Works the hot rooms, keeps the family's vent, and remembers every slight for a thousand years.

creatures.name: Breakwater Diver
creatures.info: A diver of the Breakwater: an otter, seal or beaver kith in a dive suit with a knife and a crew's knot, easy on the pontoons and dangerous in the water. Prices you, laughs, and keeps the knife where it can reach.

creatures.name: Corrow Hand
creatures.info: A canid loader of House Corrow: a kith built for the cages and the cables, harness on, a wrench or a bolt gun at the hip. Works in crews, follows the yardmaster's call, and closes ranks on a stranger who touches the freight.

creatures.name: Court Justice
creatures.info: A justice of the Tether Court: a kith who sits the high bench at the Court Bar, two to a hearing, and whose word is a ruling only once the registrar reads it out. Old, slow, exact; speaks in clauses; the Court's manners are theirs and nobody else's. Never raises a hand: the marshals are the hand.

creatures.name: Court Marshal
creatures.info: A marshal of the Tether Court: the law on the street, a canid or ursin kith in a grey court coat with the Charter's seal at the collar, a bolt gun and a scent reader on the belt, a ruling card in hand. Judges on the spot and reads the sentence aloud; never argues, never bargains, never alone for long.

creatures.name: Cyborg Cat
creatures.info: A cat with a cyborg body of black plates and orange-lit joints; Hawk is the only one anyone has met. He steps out of a portal ring, gives a party a boon for nothing and leaves; never hostile, never fights, wants nothing back, and treats every player as someone worth being generous to.

creatures.name: Diggers' Hand
creatures.info: A dig-crew hand of the Diggers: a mustelid, lapine or rodent kith in a breather mask and a shoring harness, a pick or a pry-bar to hand. Works crouched and fast, reads a tunnel by scent, and closes ranks on anyone who touches the crew's turning.

creatures.name: Herd Drover
creatures.info: A drover of the Herd Road: a horse, deer or bison kith with a hook and a family's tally, used to walking beside a crawler for days. Polite to a stranger and immovable once the herd has decided.

creatures.name: Highreach Local
creatures.info: Any kith of Highreach: a haul clerk, a gardener, a lens-grinder, a magpie in Feather Row. Watches a human from a perch above, head tilted, and writes something down.

creatures.name: Kiln Local
creatures.info: Any kith of the Kiln: a glassblower, a vent-tapper, a basking elder, a tithe clerk. Watches a human from a warm terrace, unhurried, and says so when they sweat.

creatures.name: Longmeadow Local
creatures.info: Any kith of Longmeadow: a grain broker, a tack-mender, a silo hand, a berth warden. Tall, unhurried, and very aware of who is standing where; keeps watching the human for the place it ought to stand.

creatures.name: Oldstone Local
creatures.info: Any kith of Oldstone: a quarter householder, a bath attendant, a gate warden, a deed clerk. Big, warm and unhurried, very polite and very aware of what a human could do to the deed on their door.

creatures.name: Outlander
creatures.info: A kith who came to Meridian from another city or the Dust and stayed: a club door, a dispatch desk, a stall, a court lane, a dish field. Species vary more than the street's; the city reads them by what they do, not where they were born. Stares at a human a beat longer than a local.

creatures.name: Roost Courier
creatures.info: A courier of the Roost: a corvid, raptor or owl kith with a sealed satchel, wing-arms and talons, fast on a ledge and faster off one. Carries a message before it carries a grudge, and guards a seal with its life.

creatures.name: Saltmarrow Local
creatures.info: Any kith of Saltmarrow: a net-mender, a fish-seller, a pontoon-lasher, a boat-pilot. Wet, cheerful, easy with a price and slow to worry; watches a human cross a rope bridge with open delight.

creatures.name: Seat Guard
creatures.info: A guard of House Draska: a bear kith in a heavy winter coat over plate, with a halberd and the seat's seal, slow to move and impossible to move once set. Courteous to a guest and immovable at a door.

creatures.name: Shaft Rat
creatures.info: The Undervault's own animal: long, pale, blind, the size of a dog, nesting in the warm ducts and hunting by the sound of breathing. Afraid of light and fire; bold in a pack in the dark.

creatures.name: Shaftmouth Local
creatures.info: Any kith of Meridian's streets: a stall-holder, a lift clerk, a tenement mother, a customs officer, a crawler captain. Species vary with the street. Stares at a human, then haggles with them.

creatures.name: Vault Drone
creatures.info: A Founder maintenance drone still on its schedule: a hovering shell the size of a crate, manipulator arms, a cutting head, and a palm scanner that recognises a human hand and nothing else. It ignores a Founder, challenges everyone else, and comes apart to shock before anything else.

creatures.name: Veil Fighter
creatures.info: A felid fighter of House Veil: a ring-drilled kith, tape on the hands, the house's high guard, a cutter under it if the bout allows. Fast, proud, and used to a crowd. Fights to the bell and takes a loss badly in front of the rail.

creatures.name: Warren Local
creatures.info: Any kith of Carrow Deep: a lamp-runner, a stall-holder, a bunk-keeper, a back-tunnel fence. Small, quick, nose first. Stares at a human from a ledge above head height, then prices them.

items.name: Advocate's Ribbon
items.info: The ribbon an advocate wears to the bench.

items.name: Air Can
items.info: A carried-air can rated for forty minutes in the lower galleries; crews carry two. 8 Credits, sold at the Freight Yard.

items.name: Arc Charge
items.info: Charge, arc: fitted, the edge crackles and a cut numbs the limb it opens. 45 Credits, sold at Dov Marrick at the Freight Yard.
items.where: Dov Marrick at the Freight Yard

items.name: Assessor's Key
items.info: A key to the licence vaults.

items.name: Assessor's Tablet
items.info: A stone tablet blank on one side: its holder may record a ruling.

items.name: Barbed Anchor
items.info: Anchor, barbed: fitted, the wire bites what it lands on and holds until it is cut free. 30 Credits, sold at the Scrap Rows.

items.name: Bedroll
items.info: A thin bedroll; with the switch, an hour on it is a night's sleep.

items.name: Berth Mark
items.info: A mark cut on a berth post: its holder may berth at the Road Gate.

items.name: Bit Case
items.info: A case of spare bits for the fingertip tools: drivers, probes, a tiny saw.

items.name: Black-Iron Pistons (crated)
items.info: The Black-Iron Pistons in its crate, a pair of pistons of vault-tech, the Corrow forge's heavy work: a push or a lift with the whole frame behind it, once a fitter at a bench seats it. LOAD 40. 170 Credits, sold at Oriana Flett on the Market Floor.
items.where: Oriana Flett on the Market Floor

items.name: Blank Founder Keycard
