lore.name: Blood Marks in Meridian
lore.info: Kill someone who posed no threat and the comm band carries it to every yard by the next shift, scent pulse and all; a house will not put its scent seal beside a name the boards call a killer.

lore.name: Crawlers and the Dust Road
lore.info: A crawler is the Dust's vehicle: a tracked hull on whisker-sensor arrays that read the flats through a storm, a cab built for a crouched canid driver, a hold for Corrow's manifests, muzzle masks on hooks for the air. House Corrow runs them from Wallgate's Gate Yard and carries captains it trusts on a note; Bram Tolliver's bay sells and refits them, Sera Howl's dispatch books their hauls, and Brandy Vane's gate logs every plate through the wall. A skiff takes two and one manifest; a refitted hauler takes a long hold or a gun deck under the gate's permit. The road pays in salvage and homestead freight and kills by storm; the captains who last are the ones who turn back. A human at the sticks sits upright in a cab nobody built for that, and the Founder drive-cores some old crawlers still carry wake for that hand alone.

lore.name: Crews of Meridian
lore.info: Crews of Meridian: every house runs crews and every crew holds a block and a racket. The Rail Runners (House Veil) hold Market Floor at Shaftmouth Market: the bets and a cut of every stall on the floor: the rail reads a stall's takings by scent before the boards post; the cut is 15 a day. The Cage Crew (House Corrow) hold Freight Yard at Shaftmouth Market: cage fees on every load up or down the shaft: a tally scored on the harness of whoever carried it; the cut is 15 a day. The Ring Hands (House Veil) hold The Ring at Veil Gym: the corners: who fights, who cuts and who bets, decided at a ringside stool with a tail gap; the cut is 10 a day. The Wall Crew (House Corrow) hold Scrap Rows at Wallgate: the gate: what goes out on a crawler and what comes back, read off the manifests nobody declares; the cut is 10 a day. Howl's Crew, Sera Howl's, holds nothing yet. A crew that cannot collect sends its muscle; a block under pressure goes to war; a war ends with a settlement that says who holds the block, and the street remembers which side the human took.

lore.name: District: Highreach
lore.info: Highreach. The Roost, the avian city on a mountain spur above the cloud deck: spires joined by thin bridges, open platforms and drops where other cities have stairs, wind through every room, perches where others have chairs. Corvid, raptor and owl kith run the comms, the couriers and the sky-haul, and keep the oldest records of the kith. Nothing is built at a human's reach: a human climbs, crouched against the wind. Its hub is The Landing; its other places: The Bridges, Wind Market, The Archive Spire, The Courier Steps, The Relay Crown. It joins The Tether.

lore.name: District: Longmeadow
lore.info: Longmeadow. The Herd Road, Longmeadow: the caravanserai city on the open plains past the Dust, the far end of the crawler road, wide halls on posts with no walls and no doors, grain stacks and drive yards under a sky that never ends. Deer, horse and bison kith live on grain, draft power and the road, and order themselves by the herd: who walks where, who speaks first, who eats last, all of it read by scent. A human has no place in that order at all, which unsettles Longmeadow more than claws ever have. Its hub is The Road Gate; its other places: The Long Hall, The Grain Stacks, The Drive Yards, The Council Ring, The Seed Vault. It joins The Dust.

lore.name: District: Oldstone
lore.info: Oldstone. The ursid seat, Oldstone: the oldest kith city, walled on a cold upland northwest of Meridian, on charter land the old builders deeded before the Thaw. Thick walls, heavy doors, winter halls and warm floors, every deed of the seat set in stone in the Deed Hall's walls. Bear and panda kith hold old money and the oldest court below the Tether, and every door is scent-sealed by the family that holds it. A living human can void every deed in the walls, and the whole city knows it. Its hub is The Winter Gate; its other places: The Old Quarter, The Deed Hall, The Warm Baths, The Deed Vault, The Watch Wall. It joins Shaftmouth.

lore.name: District: Saltmarrow
lore.info: Saltmarrow. The Shallows, Saltmarrow: the sea-city on a grey coast west of Meridian, a half-drowned Founder city whose streets are pontoons lashed between the tops of flooded blocks, tide stairs going down into the water, doors that open under it. Otter, seal and beaver kith live on drowned-vault salvage, the fisheries and the only sea trade, and price everything easy. Every pontoon is scent-marked by the crew that lashed it; a human who cannot swim is carried, paid, and laughed at kindly. Its hub is Pontoon Row; its other places: The Fish Market, Salvage Quay, The Tide Stair, The Breakwater Hall, The Drowned Gate. It joins Shaftmouth.

lore.name: District: Shaftmouth
lore.info: Shaftmouth. The market district around the great shaft's head, where the Undervault's salvage comes up the freight lifts and every house keeps a yard, a gym or a tab. Street level Meridian: stalls, tenements, pit gyms, comm towers and the lift queues, counters at muzzle height, tail gaps in every rail, scent-locks on every door, grooming stalls on every corner, floors kept fur-warm. Its hub is Shaftmouth Market; its other places: Veil Gym, Fang Tenement, Varga's Bench. It joins Oldstone, Saltmarrow, The Dust, The Kiln, The Tether, The Undervault.

lore.name: District: The Dust
lore.info: The Dust. The frontier past the city wall: ruin fields, homesteads on filtered water, scrap rows, and Founder installations nobody has keyed. Storms come off the flats with no warning the comms can give; the crawlers steer by whisker-sensor arrays, and the Founder doors out there are human-height boxes the crews stoop into. Its hub is Wallgate; its other places: Old Relay. It joins Longmeadow, Shaftmouth, The Warren.

lore.name: District: The Kiln
lore.info: The Kiln. Ashgrave, the Kiln: the reptile city on a geothermal field south of Meridian, vents steaming across black rock, terraces of black glass, foundries and the power plants that feed the cable. Monitor, gecko and crocodilian kith bask on warm floors and work the hot rooms a furred kith cannot stand for an hour; the Kiln's law is slow, scent-sealed and remembers a thousand years. A human sweats here, and works anyway. Its hub is The Vent Field; its other places: The Basking Galleries, The Foundry, The Glass Works, The Slow Court, The Plant Core. It joins Shaftmouth.

lore.name: District: The Tether
lore.info: The Tether. The elevator station at the top of Meridian's cable, where the corporate orbital begins: customs, licences, labs, and the courts that still read the Founder charters. Cold floors the kith work in pelt-climate suits, clean air, scent seals on every form, paperwork with teeth. Its hub is Tether Gate; its other places: . It joins Highreach, Shaftmouth.

lore.name: District: The Undervault
lore.info: The Undervault. The Founder catacombs under Meridian: cryo galleries, service tunnels, flooded transit tubes and doors that answer only to a human hand. Salvage crews work the upper levels on carried air through muzzle masks; nobody works the lower ones twice. Every room is human-height, human-cold and, to a kith, cramped. Its hub is The Deep Gallery; its other places: . It joins Shaftmouth.

lore.name: District: The Warren
lore.info: The Warren. Carrow Deep, the burrowers' city, dug into an escarpment a long day east of Wallgate: chambers and tunnels stacked inside the rock, no straight street, every turning scent-marked, markets in caverns, ceilings at a stoat's reach. Mustelid, lapine and rodent kith live on salvage and smuggling out of Founder tunnels, and keep the cheapest bunk in the world. A human stoops all day here. Its hub is The Cliff Gate; its other places: The Hollow Market, Lamplight Rows, The Diggers' Hall, The Air Works, The Deep Cut. It joins The Dust.

lore.name: Founder-speak
lore.info: The human's own language survives as Founder-speak: the Charter's clauses, machine labels, court forms, the words children learn to read the old signs with. Everyday speech is its descendant with scent-words in it. A human talking plainly sounds like a court document, and everyone hears it.

lore.name: House Ashgrave
lore.info: The clan of the Kiln: the families who tap the vents, run the plants that feed the cable, cast its iron and blow its glass, and sit the Slow Court. Ashgrave sells power, iron and glass to anyone, collects its tithes to the last coin, and settles everything by a ruling it will remember for a thousand years. Its orders are scent-sealed and its debts are posted.

lore.name: House Corrow
lore.info: The canid house that moves Meridian's freight: the great shaft's cages, the wall lifts, the crawlers into the Dust, and the clubs where its crews drink the pay. Corrow tallies what comes up the shaft before anyone else sees it, and its yardmasters' word is law on every loading floor. Its tally boards are scent tallies, its cages are built for crates and crouched loaders, and its yardmasters sign with a scent seal nobody can forge.

lore.name: House Draska
lore.info: The ursid seat of Oldstone: the bear and panda families who hold the oldest city on charter land, keep the deeds in the Deed Hall's walls and the oldest court below the Tether, and have money older than Meridian. House Draska's word is its deed and its deed is set in stone; a family's scent on a door is its title.

lore.name: House Veil
lore.info: The felid house that runs Shaftmouth's pits and the fight academies behind them: a sunken ring on every third street, a betting rail above each, and a glove for anyone who wins in front of the right people. The Veil sells spectacle and buys fighters; its runners work the Market Floor taking bets and names. A house glove is scent-taped to its fighter, and the rail reads a bout by scent before the bell: an unscented fighter is the first the Veil has ever priced.

lore.name: Running a Business in Meridian
lore.info: A business in Meridian is a lease, a house's loan and a runner's cut. The lease is signed at the Market Floor's boards; the loan comes from a house that thinks you will pay (House Veil lends through its tenants); the runner comes every tenth day for ten percent of what the business made. Pay him and the house's goodwill rises; refuse and the debt goes on the house's book. A bench that cannot pay its debt loses its premises and keeps its name. Every lease and loan carries a house's scent seal; the human signs with a palm print under a Charter clause nobody has used in a thousand years.

lore.name: Scent
lore.info: Scent is a sense the city runs on: contracts carry a scent seal, House Corrow tallies a cage by scent before the holo-board posts it, a comm carries a scent pulse with the voice, and every scanner reads a species from its scent profile. A human has none. Nobody alive has met an unscented person; it unsettles a kith more than the flat teeth do, and masking a scent is forgery under the Charter.

lore.name: Shaftmouth and the Lifts
lore.info: Shaftmouth is the market district around the great shaft's head. Everything that comes up from the Undervault lands in the Freight Yard on House Corrow's tally boards; everything bought and bet on in the district crosses the Market Floor. The freight lifts run from the shaft foot to the Lift Head, and passenger lifts from there to Tether Gate and to Wallgate. A fare is Credits on a chip. The cages are built for crates and crouched loaders, the rails have tail gaps, the counters stand at muzzle height, and the grooming stalls outnumber the food stalls two to one.

lore.name: Tech After the Founders
lore.info: The Founders' machines were kept running and everything new was built for kith use: whisker-sensor arrays on the crawlers, muzzle masks on the air cans, cage lifts sized for crates and crouched loaders, pelt-climate suits for the Tether's cold floors, claw-text controls. Flat keyboards, palm plates and human-height doorways are archaeology; only the human uses them without thinking.

lore.name: The Breakwater
lore.info: The clan of Saltmarrow: the harbour crews, divers and salvage houses who keep the sea-city afloat from the Breakwater Hall. The Breakwater lashes the pontoons, takes the harbour fee, raises the drowned salvage and prices everything easy, because the sea takes what it takes. A crew's knot and scent on a lashing is its whole claim.

lore.name: The Charter
lore.info: The Charter is the body of Founder law the Tether's court still reads: deeds, leases, access classes, the species registration every scanner runs. Nearly all the ground in Meridian is leased under it by clan-houses. A Founder's hand opens Charter locks; a Founder's name on a deed is an argument no house wants to have in court. The Charter is written in Founder-speak, the human's own language, kept for law, machine labels and court forms; deeds under it are scent-marked, and masking a scent is forgery.

lore.name: The Court and its Licences
lore.info: Every desk, bay, crawler and tower on the Tether works under a licence the Tether Court issued: a scent-sealed instrument in Founder-speak and claw-text, filed from a registered desk on the court's licensing floor and kept in a vault under the Justices' benches. A desk is registered by the court's registrar on a bond, works the registry's dockets, and files licences under its own seal; a desk whose standing with the court goes cold is audited into the cold and sealed. The houses keep corporate arms on the floors above the court's: Veil Holdings buys the licences it cannot file first, Corrow Orbital files findings against the desks that file what its cages carry. A human's palm print beside a scent seal is a signature the Charter reads and no house can forge, which is why the court registered one.

lore.name: The Day Book
lore.info: Every business keeps a Day Book: treasury, debt, stock, staff, prices. The narrator quotes the Day Book and never guesses it: the numbers come from the book's own entries each turn (the book beat), and nothing is bought, sold, hired or paid at a figure the book did not state. The book is kept in claw-text on a chip; the human keeps a second copy in Founder-speak, by hand, which every runner remarks on.

lore.name: The Diggers
lore.info: The clan of Carrow Deep: the dig crews, lamp-runners and pump-hands who cut the Warren out of the escarpment and still run it from the Long Table. The Diggers tally every turning, every pump and every haul that passes the Cliff Gate; their crews read a tunnel by scent, shore it by feel, and settle a claim by the wall's tallies and nothing else. They sell Founder salvage to anyone and owe nobody.

lore.name: The Dust
lore.info: The Dust is the frontier past Meridian's wall: ruin fields, homesteads on filtered water, scrap rows at Wallgate, and Founder installations nobody has keyed, the Old Relay among them. Storms come off the flats faster than the comms can warn, and the gate town lives behind shutters. The crawlers find their way by whisker-sensor arrays, and every Founder door out there is a human-height box the crews have to stoop into.

lore.name: The Founders
lore.info: The Founders are the people in the records who built the first of Meridian: the vaults under it, the shaft, the charters that still govern who holds which ground. Human, in the old sense: unscented, flat-toothed, built to a height every Founder doorway still keeps. They dug in, wrote the law, left the machines running, and stopped appearing. The records do not say why. A living Founder is a thing the city has no procedure for.

lore.name: The Four Trades
lore.info: A door of your own in Shaftmouth is one of four trades: a Founder-tech repair bench (Dov Marrick's crates, Ilse Varga across the street), a canteen (Marta Quell's provisions off the Scrap Rows, Orrin Vask's taproom pouring against you), a courier and freight desk at the Freight Yard (Sera Howl's cage slips, Kade Brannock's desk booking against you, Wren Calder for Corrow's cut), or a pit corner at Veil Gym (Doc Sallow's kits, Jess Marrow's corner). The trade is named when the loan is agreed and the Day Book carries it on its cover; its counter is the only one in the district built at human height.

lore.name: The Herd Road
lore.info: The clan of Longmeadow: the herd families of deer, horse and bison kith who keep the plains' grain, the drives and the far end of the crawler road, and order themselves by standing in the Council Ring. The Herd Road decides together or not at all; a family's mark and scent on a post is its whole voice.

lore.name: The Marshals
lore.info: The Marshals: the Tether Court keeps the law of Meridian through its marshals, grey-coated kith with the Charter's seal at the collar who judge on the street and carry the sentence out where they read it. Every body in the city has a file; a crime in the open, a killing, a block war fought or an unregistered reading at a lane scanner adds to it, and time, a licence on file or a fine paid at Customs Hall takes from it. The rulings run in a ladder: a fine, a turn on the holding bench in Customs Hall, ten days barred from the district, and at the top the rope, carried out on the spot. The holding bench in Customs Hall is cut with a tail gap and its floor kept coat-warm; the ruling card is raised text, read by touch before it is read aloud. The human's file is the first the Tether Court has opened on an unregistered body, and the clause the marshals rule under was written for drones.

lore.name: The Roost
lore.info: The clan of Highreach: couriers, keepers and haul clerks who run the kith's comms, carry its sealed messages and keep its oldest record in the Archive Spire. The Roost seals every message by scent, files every fact on a shelf, and settles a question by looking it up. It owns the only way up the spur, and it charges for it.

lore.name: The Stare
lore.info: A human on a Meridian street stops it. The stare is not hatred: it is a scanner reading unscented, a child who has never seen skin, a crew lead pricing what the human might carry up the shaft, a whole street that has never smelled nothing walk past. It fades district by district as the human proves themselves in each one, and the first district they prove themselves in stops staring first. Hostility, where it exists, belongs to a named person with a reason.

lore.name: The Tether
lore.info: The Tether is the elevator station at the top of Meridian's cable and the corporate orbital beyond it: customs, licences, labs with standing bids for a Founder's time, and the court that reads the Charter. Every scanner on the station reads a species off a scent profile; the human is the first thing any of them has called unscented, and the court opened a file on the word. The Tether's floors are cold enough that kith work them in pelt-climate suits; the human finds them the first comfortable rooms above the Undervault.

lore.name: The Tether Court
lore.info: The court at the top of the cable that still reads the Founder charters: registration lanes, licence desks, a licensing floor of registered desks and the Justices' benches above them. It issues the licences every house and desk on the Tether works under, keeps the registry in Founder-speak and claw-text both, and seals every instrument with a scent seal nobody can forge; the clerks work its cold floors in pelt-climate suits and sit in chairs with tail gaps.

lore.name: The Thousand Years
lore.info: Meridian is in its tenth century since the founders' day and says so the way a city says its age. A thousand years of building by kith hands made a world fitted to kith bodies: counters at muzzle height, a tail gap in every seat and rail, claw-rails up every stair, floors kept fur-warm, scent-locks on every door that is not a Founder palm plate, raised claw-text on every control face. The Founders' rooms are the only human-height spaces left, and the kith find them cramped and cold.

lore.name: The Three Theories
lore.info: Where the kith came from is argued and never settled. Seedbank: the Founders made the kith to inherit a world they were leaving. Ascension: the Founders became the kith. Inheritance: the kith came from elsewhere and found the vaults. Scholars on the Tether, house elders and street preachers each hold one, and no record settles it. A living human is evidence for all three, and an unscented one, which no theory predicted.

lore.name: The Undervault
lore.info: The Undervault is the Founder city Meridian stands on: cryo galleries, service tunnels, transit tubes under water, doors that answer only to a human hand. Salvage crews work the upper levels on carried air through muzzle masks. Vault Drones keep a Founder schedule in the lower ones. The Deep Gallery is the gallery the human woke in. Every room down here is human-height and human-cold; crews call it cramped.

lore.name: What Hurts the Kith
lore.info: Every kith body has its soft spot and its hard one, and every street fighter in Meridian knows the table by heart. Canid: chemical hurts them (a nose that reads the whole street reads a reek bomb too); cold less (a double coat). Felid: sonic hurts them (ears tuned for a whisper); bludgeoning less (they land on their feet). Ursine: burn hurts them (a pelt and fat that hold heat); slashing less (hide and fat over the ribs). Reptile: cold hurts them (cold blood slows in a cold room); slashing less (scales). Amphibian: chemical hurts them (a skin that drinks what it touches); burn less (a wet skin). Small and big-eared: sonic hurts them (big ears); chemical less (burrow-born, raised on dust and fumes). Burrower: shock hurts them (a damp coat carries a charge); piercing less (spines, plates or a hide like a boot). Hooved: shock hurts them (hooves on a wet deck carry a charge); bludgeoning less (a frame built to take a kick). Heavy hide: sonic hurts them (ears the size of doors); piercing less (a hide a bolt glances off). Bird: bludgeoning hurts them (hollow bones); cold less (down). Sea kith: burn hurts them (dry heat); cold less (blubber or the deep's cold). Chitin: chemical hurts them (breathing through the skin); slashing less (a shell). Climber: cold hurts them (thin coats built for warm canopies); bludgeoning less (a frame that falls well). A Screamer Charge deals sonic damage and a Reek Bomb deals chemical; neither troubles the unscented human much: a human nose and a human ear are dull enough to shrug both off.

Let the Archive's book take your name in the Crown Room.

quests.name: The Refit
quests.info: Bram Tolliver offers the crawler its second size: name the refit with him (a hauler bay for the long hauls, or a gun deck under Brandy Vane's permit), pay the refit from the Day Book (pay the refit), and take the crawler out of the bay with its new hatch cut at human height.
quests.goal: Take the refitted crawler out of the bay
steps: Name the refit with Bram Tolliver: a hauler bay or a gun deck.
Pay the refit from the Day Book.
Take the refitted crawler out of the bay.

quests.name: The Relay Crown
quests.info: Corwen Ashlock opens the Relay Crown's signal room for the human: climb to the Dish Deck, put a human hand on the old console's plate, and send the first call the relay has made in a thousand years to every city it can reach.
quests.goal: Send the first call from the Signal Room
steps: Climb to the Dish Deck with Corwen Ashlock.
Put your hand on the old console's plate.
Send the first call from the Signal Room.

quests.name: The Ring's Hearing
quests.info: Hollis Fenwright calls the human to the Council Ring: stand in the ring among the families' posts, answer where a thing with no place in the herd means to stand, and take the Speaker's word on the meadow hatch.
quests.goal: Take Hollis Fenwright's word on the hatch
steps: Stand in the ring among the Standing Posts.
Answer where you mean to stand.
Take Hollis Fenwright's word on the hatch.

quests.name: The Salvage Manifest
quests.info: A crawler captain at Wallgate holds a scent-sealed manifest of Founder salvage off a keyed door; bring it up the cable before Corrow's desk books it: buy or take the manifest at the Gate Yard, carry it through the Freight Yard, and file it at the Boardroom.
quests.goal: File the manifest at the Boardroom
steps: Get the manifest from the crawler captain at the Gate Yard.
Carry it through the Freight Yard without Corrow booking it.
File the manifest at the Boardroom.

quests.name: The Second Blood
quests.info: Sabine Thrace's book says the bout was fixed before Tacca ever made the bet.
quests.goal: Show Tacca Veil the fix, so the bet is void
steps: Get Sabine Thrace to open her book.
Show Tacca Veil the fix, so the bet is void.

quests.name: The Seed Kept
quests.info: The Speaker asks for the seed: carry it to the Cold Store under the oldest silo, stand in the Ring while the families walk to the stone to keep it, and seal the store with Hollis Fenwright.
quests.goal: Seal the Cold Store with Hollis Fenwright
steps: Carry the seed to the Cold Store.
Stand in the Ring while the families vote to keep it.
Seal the Cold Store with Hollis Fenwright.

quests.name: The Seed Traded
quests.info: Verity Coll wants the human's voice at the stone: make the case for trade in the Council Ring, win the families' walk to the Speaker's Stone, and load the first sacks of seed for Meridian at the Road Gate.
quests.goal: Load the first seed for Meridian at the Road Gate
steps: Make the case for trade in the Council Ring.
Win the families' walk to the Speaker's Stone.
Load the first seed for Meridian at the Road Gate.

quests.name: The Seed Vault
quests.info: With the Speaker's word, open the meadow hatch, climb down the Descent Shaft with Odile to the frosted Vault Door, put a human hand on its plate, and bring the old builders' seed up into the light.
quests.goal: Bring the seed up into the light
steps: Climb down the Descent Shaft to the Vault Door.
Put your hand on the Vault Door's plate.
Bring the seed up into the light.

quests.name: The Slow Hearing
quests.info: The shift has bought the human a hearing at the Slow Court: stand before the Stone Bench while the justices bask, answer the question the Kiln asks every stranger it owes (what are you owed), and take the bench's ruling.
quests.goal: Take the bench's ruling from Aumery Thole
steps: Stand before the Stone Bench.
Answer what you are owed.
Take the bench's ruling from Aumery Thole.

quests.name: The Storm Salvage
quests.info: A Corrow crawler went over in the flats with a hold of Founder salvage and a crouched crew of four: find it by its whisker-sensor beacon, get the crew out, and haul the hold back before Rook Haskel's crawler finds it first.
quests.goal: Haul the salvage back to the Gate Yard before Rook Haskel does
steps: Find the wreck by its beacon.
Get the crew out alive.
Haul the salvage back to the Gate Yard before Rook Haskel does.

quests.name: The Summons
quests.info: House Draska has sent for the human, and Yun Bellweather carries its summons: go northwest to Oldstone, present the summons at the Winter Gate, and stand before the heir in the Deed Hall.
quests.goal: Stand before Tova Draska in the Deed Hall
steps: Go northwest to Oldstone.
Present the summons at the Winter Gate.
Stand before Tova Draska in the Deed Hall.

quests.name: The Takeover
quests.info: The Tower's landlords want the rival of the human's trade bought out and its lease folded into theirs: make the rival an offer at their own counter, bring the rival's scent-sealed consent to the Boardroom, and sign the merged lease.
quests.goal: Sign the merged lease with Halvard Quist
steps: Make the rival an offer at their own counter.
Bring the rival's consent to the Boardroom.
Sign the merged lease with Halvard Quist.

quests.name: The Warren Run
quests.info: The Diggers of the Warren have ordered pump parts and lamp oil off Corrow's boards: load the order at the Gate Yard, run the crawler east along the escarpment road past the Old Relay, and unload at the Cliff Gate with the Diggers' tally on the manifest.
quests.goal: Get the Diggers' tally on the manifest
steps: Load the Diggers' order at the Gate Yard.
Run the crawler east to the Warren's Cliff Gate.
Get the Diggers' tally on the manifest.

quests.name: Tide Chart
quests.info: Agathe gives the diver the tide office's work.
quests.goal: Bring a diver up from the Tide Line
steps: Log the drawing tide on the Tide Stair.
Bring a diver up from the Tide Line.

quests.name: Tilda's Hive
quests.info: Highreach's keepers want Tilda Quince's bees back. Keep them hers: find the line in the Archive Spire's garden record that says the swarm was given, show it to Corwen Ashlock, and tell Tilda the hive stays on her shelf.
quests.goal: Come back to Tilda with the record and tell her the hive is hers
steps: Find the gift in the Archive's garden record.
Show the record to Corwen Ashlock.
Come back to Tilda with the record and tell her the hive is hers.

quests.name: Tunneller's Chalk
quests.info: Orsola puts the hand on Corran Sedge's crew.
quests.goal: Shore a fall in the Pump Gallery
steps: Cut a turning round the tube with Corran Sedge's crew.
Shore a fall in the Pump Gallery.

quests.name: Two Hands
quests.info: The pod's bare-frame arms are quick and light, weak, with no feel. Its log signs the maintenance locker over to its sleeper: a Founder wire rig and a Founder port, both empty, a dead service slate, and two service manipulators hanging dead from the Pod Hall's rail. Strip the manipulators, build forearms from their actuator chains, and mount the frames and the slate on them.
quests.goal: Mount the frames and the slate: the wire rig on the left forearm, the port in the right, the slate above the rig
steps: Strip two service manipulators off the Pod Hall's rail.
Build two forearms from their actuator chains.
Mount the frames and the slate: the wire rig on the left forearm, the port in the right, the slate above the rig.

quests.name: Voice's Ember
quests.info: Aumery sets the Voice's test on the galleries.
quests.goal: Speak for Ashgrave on the Glass Steps before the families
steps: Strike a binding deal basking on the Upper Terrace.
Speak for Ashgrave on the Glass Steps before the families.

quests.name: Voice's Feather
quests.info: Corwen sets the Voice's test in the market.
quests.goal: Speak for the Roost at the Lee Wall before the couriers
steps: Stop a broken seal being sold on Feather Row.
Speak for the Roost at the Lee Wall before the couriers.

quests.name: Voice's Float
quests.info: Agathe sets the Voice's test at the market.
quests.goal: Speak for the Breakwater on Tank Row
steps: Bring a back-trade crate under the harbour fee.
Speak for the Breakwater on Tank Row.

quests.name: Voice's Freight Seal
quests.info: Sera puts the Voice's seal on the table.
quests.goal: Hold the Freight Yard through a storm shift
steps: Stop a dropping cage with a brake call.
Hold the Freight Yard through a storm shift.

quests.name: Voice's Lamp
quests.info: Orsola sets the Voice's test in the market.
quests.goal: Speak for the Warren at the Lamp Well before the market
steps: Bring a back-tunnel trade under the Diggers' tally.
Speak for the Warren at the Lamp Well before the market.

quests.name: Voice's Ring Pass
quests.info: Tacca sets the Voice's test on the Market Floor.
quests.goal: Bring the floor's takings to House Veil
steps: Stage a bout on the Market Floor.
Bring the floor's takings to House Veil.

quests.name: Yard Key
quests.info: Sera sends the prospect to the wall.
quests.goal: Carry the gate town's freight manifest to Sera Howl
steps: Ride a crawler to the Old Relay and back.
Carry the gate town's freight manifest to Sera Howl.

text.homeSay: The exact words that ride the lift, swear you to a House, run your business and keep you out of a cell.
text.homeMap: Every district on one map: find a place, show one district.
text.ledePeople: Everyone Meridian introduces you to, with where to find them.
text.ledePlaces: The vaults, markets, towers and cities of Meridian and beyond.
text.ledeCreatures: The people of Meridian and what you might end up fighting.
text.ledeLore: History, the Founders, the Charter and places of Meridian.
text.ledeMechanics: How the world works, as the guide books every new character carries explain it.
text.ledeMusic: The soundtrack of Meridian, by the mood of the scene.
text.ledeDistricts: The districts of Meridian, all on the one map.
text.ledeSay: The lines that set off the world's systems.
text.ledeFactions: The Houses, crews, labs and courts you can swear to, work for or cross.
text.ledeItems: Weapons, armour, limbs, rigs, tools and goods: what each gives, the slot it takes and how you get it.
text.guideSay: Most of the world's systems listen for plain lines.
text.plannerLede: Every pick the creator offers, in its order, with the same unlocks and exclusions. The totals add up what your picks give.
text.benchLede: Build the exact line to type, then run it through the world's own crafting triggers, the same code the game runs, to see what the narrator will be told.

patter: Ladies, gentlemen, and that cryo pod that won't stop beeping:
patter.people: Everyone in the building, and a few who came in through the roof!
patter.places: Every stage in the house, front of house to the trapdoors!
patter.factions: Pick a side! Pick two! Dreamer once picked them all.
patter.creatures: Mind who you meet, folks. Most of them mean well. Some of them clap.
patter.lore: Gather round for the long version, with all the voices!
patter.abilities: The tricks of the trade, and what each one costs!
patter.traits: Pick your costume! It changes everything!
patter.items: Props, every one! Handle with care, return by morning.
patter.starts: Curtain up! Where would you like the story to begin?
patter.quests: Odd jobs for brave volunteers! Dreamer has volunteered you.
patter.map: The whole tour on one page! Dreamer has been everywhere twice.
patter.skills: Practice makes the act! Here is what to practise.
patter.say: Say the magic words. No, really, these exact ones.
patter.planner: Build your act before the curtain goes up!
patter.districts: Every neighbourhood on the tour, each with its own crowd!
patter.guide: First time at the show? Dreamer will walk you in.
patter.search: Lost something? Dreamer finds things. Sometimes the right things.
